rows: Rue du Haut-Pavé, with the Panthéon in the Distance
Charles Marville photographed a narrow street in Paris with the dome of the Panthéon rising in the distance. He was recording old streets before new boulevards replaced them.
Why is the street so empty?
Ruins of Columbia, South Carolina
George Barnard photographed the burned ruins of Columbia, South Carolina, from the Capitol in 1865. Much of the city was destroyed by fire when Sherman's army arrived in February.
What would you do if your town were burned?
Northern Railway, Paris to Compiègne
Édouard Baldus photographed a stretch of the Northern Railway at Chantilly. He recorded the new railways that crossed France, which changed travel.
How did railways change the way people lived?
Courtyard of the Imperial Stagecoach Company
Charles Marville photographed the busy yard of the Messageries Impériales, the stagecoach company in Paris, around 1865. Coaches and horses crowd the yard.
What would the yard have sounded like?
Sangor, Temple and Lake
Francis Frith photographed a temple beside a lake in India in about 1865. Frith had traveled to India to build a stock of pictures.
How does the temple look in the water?
High Bridge, Appomattox, Virginia

Timothy O'Sullivan photographed the High Bridge in Virginia, a long railroad bridge burned in the last days of the Civil War. General Lee's army was escaping west when the bridge was set on fire in April 1865.
Why would soldiers burn a bridge as they leave?
Richmond from Gamble's Hill
Alexander Gardner photographed the ruins of Richmond from Gamble's Hill in April 1865. The burned downtown stretches toward the James River.
What would you see if you looked at the city from a hill?
Ruins of the Richmond and Danville Railroad Bridge
Gardner photographed the burned bridge in Richmond. After the fire, the bridge piers stood in the river like broken teeth.
What do broken bridge piers look like?
Gettysburg Camp of Captain Huft
Alexander Gardner photographed a camp near Gettysburg in 1863. The tents and a few soldiers show how soldiers lived in the field.
What would you pack for a camp?
Mr. and Miss Constable
Oscar Rejlander photographed a man and a young woman named Constable in the 1860s. Rejlander was a gifted portrait photographer who liked natural poses.
How are the two posed together?
Mary Fisher
Julia Margaret Cameron photographed Mary Fisher in 1867. Mary was a close friend and relative who sat for her many times.
Why would Cameron photograph the same person again and again?
English Tourists at the Mer de Glace, Chamonix
Auguste Garcin photographed English tourists walking on the Mer de Glace glacier at Chamonix in 1867. Tourism in the Alps was booming, and visitors wore long dresses and hats to walk on the ice.
What would you wear on a glacier?
Festival of Ismail Pasha on Board the Ships
Gustave Le Gray photographed a party on a ship hosted by Ismail Pasha, the ruler of Egypt, in 1867. Le Gray had gone to Egypt and made pictures there for the court.
Why would a ruler throw a party on a ship?
Matra Reinhard

Jacques-Philippe Potteau photographed working-class girls such as Matra Reinhard in 1868. The pictures were made for scientists who were studying different types of people, and the girls had to stay quite still.
How do you think the sitters felt about the scientists?
Rue du Chat-qui-Pêche, Paris
Charles Marville photographed the narrowest street in Paris, called the Street of the Cat Who Fishes, in 1868. It is only about two meters wide.
How could two people pass in a street that narrow?
Gorges du Tarn, Castelbouc
Amédée Trantoul photographed the village of Castelbouc in the gorge of the Tarn River in southern France. Cliffs tower on both sides.
How would you feel living at the bottom of a canyon?
The Colossi of Memnon, Thebes
Henri Béchard photographed the two enormous seated statues of Pharaoh Amenhotep III at Thebes, Egypt. The statues have been looking over the plain for more than 3,000 years.
How would you carve a statue as big as a house?
Canyon Wall, O'Sullivan's Survey
Timothy O'Sullivan photographed canyons and deserts in the American West in 1871 during an army survey. His pictures show landscapes that many people had never imagined.
What would you pack for a trip into the desert?
Death Valley
Timothy O'Sullivan photographed Death Valley in California in 1871, the hottest place in North America. His picture shows pale sand and a few lonely tracks.
How would you cross a place that is so hot?
Alpine Lake, Sierra Nevada
Timothy O'Sullivan photographed a high mountain lake in the Sierra Nevada in California in 1871. The still water mirrors the peaks and sky.
How does the lake match the mountains?
Black Canyon of the Colorado River
In 1871 O'Sullivan took a boat up the Colorado River through Black Canyon with a survey team and photographed the walls. He had to haul a darkroom boat through rapids.
How would you make a darkroom on a boat?
Near the Mouth of the Diamond River
O'Sullivan photographed the area near where the Diamond River meets the Colorado in 1871. The rocks stand like walls around the water.
What do you see in the rock walls?
Baron Taylor
Nadar photographed Baron Isidore Taylor, a French art patron who founded groups to help artists. In the 1870s Taylor was an old man with a famous white beard.
Why would someone found a group to help artists?
George Duckworth
Julia Margaret Cameron photographed George Duckworth, a young man who would be the stepbrother of Virginia Woolf. Cameron photographed her relatives and neighbors in the 1870s.
What do you notice about the lighting?
Mrs. Rachel Gurney
Cameron photographed Mrs. Rachel Gurney in 1872, a friend, with deep shadows and soft focus. Cameron's pictures were praised by artists but criticized by some for being blurry.
Why would an artist choose to blur a picture?
Julia and Ethel Arnold
Lewis Carroll photographed the Arnold sisters in 1872. He liked to take pictures of children and often photographed his friends' daughters.
What do you think the sisters thought of Carroll?
Looking South into the Grand Canyon
William H. Bell photographed the Grand Canyon from the north rim in 1872. His photograph shows a huge cliff and the Colorado River far below.
How would it feel to stand at the rim?
Hôtel de Ville, Paris, After the Fire
Charles Marville photographed the Paris town hall after it was burned in May 1871 by the Paris Commune. Only the stone shell was left, with empty windows.
What happens to a city after a fire?
Expression of the Emotions, Plate I
This photograph was published in Charles Darwin's 1872 book The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals. Darwin used photographs to show how feelings look on faces.
What feeling do you think the picture shows?
Autograph Letter
Julia Margaret Cameron's handwriting appears in a note on a photograph. She often wrote on the mounts of her pictures and signed them as autographs.
Why would an artist write on her own photographs?
A Creeper in the Peradeniya Gardens, Ceylon
Scowen and Company photographed a twisting vine in the botanic gardens of Peradeniya in Sri Lanka. The giant baroque loops of the vine look like sculpture.
What does the vine look like?
Entrance to the Nata Dewale Grounds, Kandy
Scowen and Company photographed the entrance to a temple site in Kandy, Sri Lanka. Kandy was the last capital of the old kings of Sri Lanka.
What would a visitor see on entering?
Fruit Sellers
Scowen and Company photographed fruit sellers in Ceylon, as part of a set of local jobs. Photographs of people at work were popular souvenirs.
What fruits do you think they sold?
Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, around 1875
This is a photograph of Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, who wrote as Lewis Carroll. He was a mathematician at Oxford and a very good photographer.
What do you think about the author of Alice looking at you?
Maharaja Scindia, Nobles and High Officials, Gwalior
Raja Deen Dayal photographed the Maharaja of Scindia with nobles and officials at Gwalior in 1877. The group wears rich turbans and jackets.
How can you tell which person is the ruler?
The Viceregal Council
Raja Deen Dayal photographed the viceroy's council at a great meeting in Delhi in 1877. The viceroy governed British India, and the grand event drew hundreds of officials.
Why would so many people travel for one meeting?
Lord William Beresford's Horses
Deen Dayal photographed the prized horses of Lord William Beresford in 1877. Beresford was an officer who loved horse racing.
Which horse looks the fastest?
Rue d'Hautpoul, Entrance to the Quarries
Charles Marville photographed the entrance to old stone quarries under Paris in 1877. The city was built from stone mined beneath its streets.
What do you think is under a city?
Overview of the Quarries, Rue de Compans
Marville photographed the area of old quarries and a new market in Paris. As the city grew, it built on top of its old mines.
Why would a city build over a quarry?
Eugène Viollet-le-Duc
Nadar photographed Eugène Viollet-le-Duc, the architect who restored Notre-Dame cathedral in Paris. He rebuilt towers and added the spire.
What does an architect who rebuilds castles do all day?
General Roberts and Staff
John Burke photographed General Frederick Roberts and his staff during the Second Anglo-Afghan War in 1878. Roberts led the march to Kabul.
What do the soldiers' uniforms look like?
River Gorge Above Lalpura
John Burke photographed a river gorge near Lalpura on the Kabul River in 1878. The cliffs rise on both sides of the water.
What would crossing the gorge be like?
Landi Kotal, the Camp
John Burke photographed the army camp at Landi Kotal in the Khyber Pass in 1878. Tents stretch across the high valley.
Why would a camp be set up in a pass?
Chinak, Looking Toward the Kurram River
John Burke photographed the area near the Kurram River in Afghanistan in 1878. The wide valley is marked by mountains in the distance.
How far do you think the mountains are?
Couple Portrait on Enamel
Étienne Carjat, a celebrated Paris photographer, made this portrait of a couple. They paid extra to have it fired onto enamel, a more permanent finish.
Why would they want their portrait to last longer?
Bernt Askevold
This is a portrait of Bernt Askevold, a Norwegian painter, around 1880. Many of these portraits were saved by regional archives in Norway.
Why would an archive keep old portraits?
Roald Amundsen at Eight
This photograph shows Roald Amundsen as an eight-year-old boy around 1880. He grew up to be the first person to reach the South Pole in 1911.
What do you think a polar explorer looked like as a child?
Boy with a Rocking Horse
A boy poses with his rocking horse in a Norwegian photo studio around 1880. Studios had toy horses as props for children.
What toy would you bring?
Boys in Matching Outfits
Two boys in matching outfits pose in a Norwegian studio around 1880. Brothers were often dressed alike for portraits.
Why would parents dress brothers the same?
Group on a Beach with Three Babies
This ferrotype, a photograph on thin metal, shows a group with three babies on a beach around 1880. Beach photographers set up tents to make quick portraits for visitors.
How would a photographer work on a beach?
Girl in a Checked Dress
A seated girl in a checked dress poses in a Norwegian studio. Her dress pattern shows how clothes looked in the 1880s.
How does the checked pattern look in a black-and-white picture?
Church of the Holy Sepulchre, Jerusalem
Luigi Fiorillo photographed a religious ceremony at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem in the 1880s. Pilgrims from around the world came to this holy place.
Why would people travel so far?
Billy the Kid
This tintype of the outlaw Billy the Kid was taken around 1880 in New Mexico. It is the only authenticated photograph of him, and he holds a rifle and wears a hat. He was killed in 1881 at age 21.
Why do people remain fascinated by outlaws?
Likely Patrick J. Norton and Siblings
This photograph shows a family of children, most likely Patrick Norton and his siblings, around 1885. Studio portraits like this were treasured by families.
What do you think the children are feeling?
A Broadman's Cottage
Peter Henry Emerson photographed a cottage of a Norfolk Broads worker in 1886. Platinum prints give a soft, lasting gray tone.
What would living on the Broads be like?
A Norfolk Boat-Yard
Emerson photographed a boat-yard on the Norfolk Broads in 1886. Workers build wooden boats, which are used to carry reeds and cargo.
How would you build a wooden boat?
Gathering Water-Lilies
Emerson photographed people gathering water-lilies from a boat on the Norfolk Broads in 1886. Lilies were collected for sale as decorations.
Why would people collect water-lilies?
Gunner Working Up to Fowl
Emerson photographed a wildfowl hunter creeping toward ducks in a punt on the Broads in 1886. Hunters had to be very quiet to get near.
How would you sneak up on a bird?
Poling the Marsh Hay
Emerson photographed men poling a boat loaded with marsh hay on the Norfolk Broads in 1886. Hay was cut from the wetlands and carried by boat.
Why was a boat better than a cart in the marsh?
A Marsh Farm
Emerson photographed a farm in the marsh of Norfolk in 1886. Flat land and pale sky show how big the open land is.
What would farming a marsh be like?
An Autumn Morning
Emerson photographed a misty autumn morning in the English countryside in 1886. He used soft focus to match the way the human eye sees.
What do you hear on a misty morning?
Twixt Land and Water
Thomas Frederick Goodall, a friend of Emerson, helped make this picture of a boat in the shallow water of the Broads in 1886. The title means between land and water.
Where does the land end and the water begin?
In the Barley Harvest
Emerson photographed workers bringing in the barley harvest in the 1880s. He disliked posed pictures, and this one shows ordinary work.
What jobs can you see?
Picnic Party, Mashobra
Raja Deen Dayal photographed a picnic party in Mashobra near Shimla in 1887. British officials and their families held lavish outdoor parties in the hills.
What would you bring to a picnic in the hills?
Robert Hotz and His Bulldog
Raja Deen Dayal photographed Robert Hotz, a professional photographer, with his bulldog in 1887. Hotz was a competitor who lived in Shimla.
Why would a photographer pose with his dog?
Colonel Thuillier and His Wife Emmeline
Deen Dayal photographed Colonel Thuillier and his wife Emmeline in 1887. Large group portraits and couples brought him regular work.
What can you tell about the couple?
Decayed Fishermen
Emerson photographed old fishermen at a hospital for retired fishermen in Great Yarmouth in 1887. The men sit quietly in their uniform and caps.
What stories might the old fishermen tell?
Confessions
Emerson photographed a scene called Confessions in his book Pictures from Life in Field and Fen in 1887. He used everyday people and a natural, quiet look.
What do you think the title means?
Church of Saint-Julien, Brioude
Édouard Baldus made a photogravure, a print from a photograph, of the Romanesque church of Saint-Julien in Brioude, France. Photogravures turned photographs into ink prints for books.
How could you make a printed book from a photograph?
Man Bicycling
Étienne-Jules Marey photographed a man on a bicycle in motion around 1890. Marey, a scientist, invented the chronophotograph that records movement in a single plate.
How does the camera show motion in one picture?
Mount Washington, Massachusetts
Robert Stuart Redfield photographed Mount Washington in Massachusetts on July 22, 1890. Redfield was a leading amateur of his day, and he later became a driving force of art photography.
What time of year do you think this is?
Fish Porters
Paul Géniaux photographed porters carrying baskets of fish in the 1890s. Géniaux took many pictures of working people in France.
How heavy would the baskets be?
Jain Temple, Calcutta
A. W. A. Plâté Studio photographed the Jain Temple in Calcutta, now Kolkata, in the 1890s. The temple is decorated with mirrors, glass and gardens.
What does a temple look like when it is covered in mirrors?
Marsh Weeds
Peter Henry Emerson photographed reeds and weeds on the marsh for a book of etchings from photographs in 1890. His late work was softer and more artistic.
How do soft pictures feel different?
A Winter's Sunrise
Emerson's last book of photographs, Marsh Leaves, included this winter sunrise. He used a delicate gravure to catch the sky.
What time is it in the picture?
Snapshot from My Window, Berlin
Alfred Stieglitz photographed a snowy street from his window in Berlin around 1890. Stieglitz, who studied there, loved the changing light and weather.
What can you see from your window?
Thomas Smillie
Thomas Smillie was the Smithsonian Institution's first photographer. He photographed objects, scientists and expeditions for the museum.
Why would a museum need its own photographer?
Honus Wagner
This tintype shows Honus Wagner, who would become one of baseball's greatest shortstops. Wagner started playing professionally in the 1890s.
Why would a baseball star's old tintype be treasured?
Hohen-Kasten, Appenzell

The Detroit Publishing Company made this photochrom of Hohen Kasten, a mountain in Appenzell, Switzerland, in the 1890s. A photochrom turns a black-and-white photograph into a color print using lithographic stones.
How could color be added to a black-and-white picture?
The Clock Tower, Bern
This photochrom shows the Zytglogge clock tower in Bern, Switzerland. The tower has a clock with moving figures that put on a show every hour.
What would you see when the clock strikes?
The Urseren Valley, Andermatt
A photochrom shows the Urseren Valley, a high Alpine valley in Switzerland, with green meadows and mountains. Photochroms made the Alps look like paintings.
What do you notice about the colors?
Devil's Bridge, Andermatt
This Detroit Publishing photochrom shows the Devil's Bridge in the Schöllenen Gorge in Switzerland. Legend says the Devil built it in exchange for the first soul to cross.
Would you cross a bridge built by the Devil?
General View, Aberdovey, Wales
A photochrom of the seaside town of Aberdovey in Wales in the 1890s. Photochrom prints were sold to tourists as vivid souvenirs.
What do you think a day at the beach in 1890 was like?
